reference.shortdesc: A map reference is a mechanism for referencing a DITA map from a DITA map.

section.title: Usage information
section.p: The mapref element is a convenience element. It is equivalent to a topicref element with the format attribute set to ditamap.

section.title: Processing expectations
section.p: See How relationship tables establish linking relationships for information about how relationship tables in nested maps are handled.

section.title: Specialization hierarchy
section.p: The mapref element is specialized from topicref. It is defined in the mapgroup-domain module.

div.p: The following attributes are available on this element: , , , impose-role, keyref, and keys.

For this element:
The format attribute has a default value of ditamap.
The impose-role attribute has a fixed value of keeptarget.

example.title: Example
example.p: The following code sample shows how a mapref element can be used to reference a submap. The base-elements.ditamap document references the map-group-elements.ditamap:
The map-group-elements.ditamap document contains references to the element-reference topics for the map group domain. It is constructed as a map in order to enable easy editing of the child topics.
example.codeblock: <map> <title>Map group elements</title> <topicref keyref="mapgroup-d" > <topicref keyref="keydef" /> <topicref keyref="mapref" /> <topicref keyref="topicgroup" /> <topicref keyref="topichead" /> </topicref> </map>
example.p: After processing, the base-elements.ditamap contains the topic references that originally were located in the submap:
example.codeblock: <map> <title>Base elements</title> <!-- ... --> <topicref href="containers/domain-elements.dita" > <!-- ... --> <topicref keyref="mapgroup-d" > <topicref keyref="keydef" /> <topicref keyref="mapref" /> <topicref keyref="topicgroup" /> <topicref keyref="topichead" /> </topicref> <!-- ... --> </topicref> <!-- ... --> </map>
